subject: Discovery Recap & PoC Plan — Integration + Onboarding (FastRetail)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery Recap & PoC Plan — Integration + Onboarding (FastRetail)

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. Feel free to flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- Search latency spikes during peak promotions (95th percentile often > 1.2s).
- High per-token cost for customer-facing ranking/generation flows.
- Lack of observability across model calls (hard to attribute cost to features).
- Need for on-prem / VPC options for sensitive customer PII workflows.

Current stack summary you described:
- Frontend: React micro-frontends calling backend APIs.
- Backend: Java/Node services, embeddings stored in Pinecone, current model calls to OpenAI API (gpt-4 style).
- Identity: Okta for SSO.

Success criteria for the PoC (as discussed):
- Latency: reduce 95th percentile inference latency for search reranking to <= 500ms.
- Cost: reduce model-related per-user cost by ~30% at target QPS.
- Observability: token-level cost and latency breakdown per API route.
- Security: support VPC deployment or customer-managed key options for the PoC dataset.

Proposed PoC & onboarding plan (timeline):
Week 0 (this week): sign-off on PoC scope and NDA/contract redlines.
Week 1: Technical kickoff — integration of Redwood SDK (Python/Node) into a staging service + test corpus ingest.
Week 2: Run test workload, gather latency/cost baselines, enable prefix/KV caching.
Week 3: Tuning: batching/quantization suggestions, rerun benchmarks.
Week 4: Evaluation: compare success criteria; decision point to expand to canary production.

Owners:
- Redwood commercial: Ben Carter (me) — contract and scope.
- Redwood CS/onboarding: Marissa Cole — onboarding & success metrics.
- Redwood SE: Jonas Weber — technical integration and performance tuning.
- FastRetail: Alex Chen — product owner; Priya Natarajan (ops) — technical lead.

Next steps (asks):
1) Alex: confirm success criteria above and add any missing acceptance criteria.
2) FastRetail ops: share a short sample workload or representative logs for week 1 testing (S3 link preferred).
3) Internal (Marissa/Jonas): prepare integration checklist and PoC plan PDF — I’ll attach the preliminary plan in a follow-up.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a proposed kickoff calendar invite after Alex confirms availability.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

- SDKs: we’ll need official support for Python (backend) and Node (edge service). Java would be nice-to-have but not required for the PoC.
- Data residency: for the PoC we can use staging in us-west; production will need EU/US regional controls depending on customer cohort.
- Security: we need to validate SSO integration (Okta) and confirm whether Redwood supports SAML/OIDC + optional customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).

Acceptance criteria: I added a data security bullet: Redwood must demonstrate isolation of customer data in the PoC and provide an evidence doc for audit purposes (SOC2 artifacts or equivalent).

I’ll ask Priya to pull a small log sample and an anonymized dataset (S3 link) — she’ll try to get that by Tuesday.

Availability: I’m available for a kickoff on Tue Nov 17 afternoon PT or Wed Nov 18 morning PT.

Alex — quick technical note from the SE side to make the kickoff smoother. High-level compatibility and quickstarts below.

Supported SDKs / languages for PoC:
- Python (recommended for backend ingestion & batch scoring) — pip package: redwood==0.6.2
- Node (recommended for edge routing and low-latency calls) — npm: @redwood/inference
- Java SDK (beta) — available on request

API compatibility:
- Redwood offers an OpenAI-compatible REST surface for text generation and embeddings, plus an extended /v1/streams endpoint for low-latency streaming. Authentication is API-key based; for Private deployments we support mTLS and token introspection with Okta.

Integration checklist highlights:
- Obtain staging API key and create environment config (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_ENV).
- Ingest sample corpus to staging S3/Blob and register as test index.
- Implement prefix/KV caching in node edge service (we’ll share recommended cache TTLs).
- Enable token-level logging and send a brief sample to the observability dashboard for validation.

Sample snippet (Node):
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'rw-instruct-1', prompt: '...'});

For the PoC load test (200 rps spike) we recommend starting with a 1 GPU dedicated instance and adding burst capacity; we’ll tune batching/quantization during week 2.

I propose a technical kickoff Tue Nov 17 13:00 PT — we’ll use this time to validate SSO, hand over API keys, and walk through a quick integration demo. If logistics change, I can move to Wed morning.

-Jonas
